title: fix: use fuzzy match for internal clearEditorHistory automation command (build fix for vscode-engineering#3718)

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

body:
## Build failure

The `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` smoke tests (`Run smoke tests (Electron)`) failed identically on Windows, Linux, and macOS with:

```
QuickAccess.runCommand(commandId: workbench.action.clearEditorHistoryWithoutConfirm, match: exactCommandId) failed to find command.
  at QuickAccess.runCommand (test/automation/out/quickaccess.js)
  at async QuickAccess.openFileQuickAccessAndWait
  at async QuickAccess.openFile
```

The failure originates from `QuickAccess.openFile` -> `openFileQuickAccessAndWait`, which internally clears editor history before opening a file. On macOS this also cascaded into a `Language Features > verifies quick outline (js)` timeout via the same broken quick-access path.

## Root cause

`test/automation/src/quickaccess.ts` `runCommand` gained a `CommandMatchMode` option whose default is now `exactCommandId`. That mode matches the focused quick-pick entry via `element.id === commandId`, where `element.id` is read from the new `data-quick-input-id` DOM attribute set by `QuickPickItemElementRenderer.renderElement` in `src/vs/platform/quickinput/browser/quickInputList.ts`.

The `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` tests first launch an **older stable build** of VS Code. `openFileQuickAccessAndWait` runs `clearEditorHistoryWithoutConfirm` against that stable build, which does **not** emit the `data-quick-input-id` attribute. As a result `element.id` is `undefined`, the `exactCommandId` match never succeeds, and the command is reported as not found after all retries.

Several call sites were updated to `match: 'exactLabel'` for backward compatibility, but this internal call inside `openFileQuickAccessAndWait` was not, so it silently regressed to the new default `exactCommandId` against builds that cannot satisfy it.

## How the fix works

The internal call passes a command **id** (`workbench.action.clearEditorHistoryWithoutConfirm`) as the palette query. The command-palette filter already narrows results to exactly that command when the `>`-prefixed id is typed, so a strict id/label DOM match is unnecessary here. Switching this single call to `match: 'fuzzy'` restores the pre-regression behavior — accepting the focused entry once the palette has filtered down — and works against both stable and insiders builds regardless of whether the new `data-quick-input-id` metadata is present.

Only the internal history-clearing helper is changed; other call sites that always run against the current build continue to use `exactCommandId`/`exactLabel` as intended. No product code or telemetry is affected.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back.**

Public culprit: commit `e2b48f58` — PR microsoft/vscode#332892 ("Launch Skill: Quick Pick should expose item IDs for automation").

Rationale: The culprit change is broadly useful (it adds automation-facing item ids) and touches many files; a full revert would discard that value. The regression is a single missed call site in test automation, and this fix-forward is bounded, low-risk, and restores green without cross-repository work. A revert should only be preferred if this fix-forward cannot land promptly.

Owners to consult: `@jruales`

## Validation

The change is confined to `test/automation/src/quickaccess.ts` and uses the existing, already-typed `'fuzzy'` value of `CommandMatchMode`. TypeScript compilation and the smoke-test suite could not be run in this environment because build tooling/dependencies are not installed here. The fix is verified by source inspection: the internal call no longer depends on the `data-quick-input-id` attribute that older builds lack, which is the exact condition that produced the failure.

## Risk

Low. Only test-automation code changes. The `fuzzy` match restores the behavior this call had before PR #332892, and the `>`-prefixed command-id query filters the palette to the single intended command, so accepting the focused entry is safe.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@jruales`

title: debug: work around frozen renderer when launching from Run and Debug
body:
> **Authored by GitHub Copilot** on behalf of @jruales. Draft — temporary workaround, not a product change.

## Problem

Launching the workbench with the **VS Code** or **Renderer and Main processes** compound can leave the window painted but completely unresponsive: nothing is clickable, the keyboard does nothing, the command palette opens but neither responds nor dismisses, and the extension host never finishes starting.

The renderer is stuck in the debugger's *waiting-for-debugger* state. Confirmed on a stuck window:

- `Runtime.evaluate` of synchronous code succeeds
- `setTimeout` and `requestAnimationFrame` never fire; event handlers never run
- `Debugger.resume` returns `Can only perform operation while paused`
- `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger` immediately restores the window

## Cause (upstream, in js-debug)

`Inspector.workerScriptLoaded` — a Blink event fired when a web worker finishes evaluating — can arrive for a session js-debug hasn't registered yet, because `targetCreated` is queued through `enqueueLifecycleFn` while workers such as `editorWorkerService` start immediately. js-debug throws on unknown session ids, the throw escapes `EventEmitter.fire` leaving its delivery queue populated, and every later `fire` then returns without dispatching. That permanently kills the CDP message pump, so `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger` is never sent.

```
Error: Unknown session id: B9878282765DBAAB165E4A5851627507 while processing: Inspector.workerScriptLoaded
    at ut._onMessage (.../ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js:58:8166)
    at U.fire        (.../ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js:39:11654)
```

Reported as microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2401, fix proposed in microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2402.

## This change

Adds a hidden `Resume Stuck Renderer` configuration to the two affected compounds. It waits 8s so js-debug can attach normally, then resumes the renderer only if its event loop never turns. It is inert on a healthy renderer.

## Validation

Root cause and fix confirmed by a controlled A/B: js-debug built with and without the upstream fix, loaded into a real VS Code Insiders window via `--extensionDevelopmentPath`, same machine, repo, profile and launch compound.

| js-debug build | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Unpatched | Workbench freezes. Reproduced repeatedly. |
| Patched | Works every time. |

Not environment-specific: it also reproduces with a completely empty Code OSS profile, and `.build/electron` matches the pinned `42.8.1`. It is timing-sensitive, so it may not reproduce on every machine.

The workaround itself was verified to stay silent against a healthy renderer and to log `Resumed renderer that was waiting for the debugger` against a deliberately stalled one.

## Notes for reviewers

- Draft, and intended to be **reverted** once microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2402 ships in the bundled js-debug.
- Written as `.ts` rather than `.js` to satisfy the pre-commit check; Node runs it directly via type stripping.
- Port `9222` is hardcoded to match `Launch VS Code Internal`.

title: Fix sign-in dead-end in installed web apps (PWA)
body: Signing in from an installed web app (PWA) dead-ends: tapping **Continue with GitHub** shows *"The browser blocked opening a new tab or window"*, no sign-in window appears, and the **Retry** button is covered by the "Signing in…" modal so it cannot even be pressed. ## Cause Browsers only allow `window.open` while a click's user activation is still live. Chat sign-in does a lot between the click and the open — shows a dialog, activates the authentication extension, requests an authorization URL over the network — so by the time it opens anything the gesture has expired and the window is refused. In a browser tab this is survivable: the prompt appears and **Retry** works, because Retry runs inside a fresh click. In an installed web app there is no tab to fall back to, and the prompt is unreachable, so sign-in cannot be completed at all. Measured on an iPhone PWA, `window.open()` succeeds inside a real tap and is refused outside one: | call | inside a tap | outside a tap | | --- | --- | --- | | `window.open()` | ✅ | ❌ | | `window.open(url, '_blank')` | ✅ | ❌ | | `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener')` | ❌ | ❌ | (`noopener` is refused even inside a tap — an installed app has no independent browsing context to hand it to.) ## Change Claim the window synchronously on the click, then navigate that reserved window once the URL is known. - `reserveWindowForExternalOpen()` opens the window during the click and shows a short placeholder, since the window is visible immediately but the URL may be a second or more away. - `windowOpenWithSuccess()` consumes the reservation if there is one, and otherwise behaves exactly as before. - `releaseReservedWindowForExternalOpen()` closes the window when setup ends without using it. `close()` is not always honoured — an in-app browser view can ignore it — so if the window survives it is given a short explanation rather than left blank on top of the app. Gated on `isStandalone() || isSafari`: installed apps fail this way in whichever browser installed them, and Safari blocks the popup in tabs too. Everywhere else popups still work after the gesture, so nothing is reserved and behaviour is unchanged. ## Testing - Verified on an iPhone PWA that the sign-in window now opens on tap with no warning dialog. Full end-to-end sign-in still needs a host where the `github-authentication` extension loads; a local tunnel cannot exercise it. - Placeholder rendering, navigation of the reserved window, `close()`, and the refuses-to-close fallback verified in WebKit. - `tsc` and `eslint` clean. Draft while the end-to-end run on insiders is pending.

title: agentHost: avoid duplicate subagents on reconnect
body:
- Reconnecting to an active Agent Host turn used two independent progress producers: activeTurnToProgress created a one-shot snapshot while _observeTurn replayed and continued observing the same response parts. This made correctness depend on manually keeping snapshot adoption, emitted text lengths, and response-part offsets synchronized.

- A settled subagent tool exposed the weakness because the snapshot rendered a serialized parent invocation, while the live observer still needed to run to attach the child chat and forward its activity. That observer could emit a second live parent invocation, leaving the serialized snapshot without live metadata or navigation while the second card worked normally.

- Make the reactive turn observer the only reconnect progress producer. Its synchronous first pass already replays accumulated response parts before the session is returned, and subsequent updates now mutate the same live invocation instead of competing with a disconnected snapshot.

- Preserve Restore Checkpoint behavior when the observer synchronously replays file edits before the ChatModel exists. Queue those edits per session and flush them into AgentHostSnapshotController when the matching model is created.

- Add reconnect regressions for completed subagent tools, completed file edits, settled tools followed by streaming markdown, streaming tool transitions, and owned client tools. These assert that reconnect renders exactly one invocation while retaining child-chat updates and checkpoint data.

title: agentHost: add regression tests that the auto-approve policy does not clamp the Autopilot mode axis
body:
### Background

#321865 moved Agent Host Autopilot off the `autoApprove` approvals axis onto the independent `mode` axis (`mode='autopilot'`; the `autoApprove` enum is now `default | assisted | autoApprove`).

The enterprise managed setting `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` forces the `ChatToolsAutoApprove` policy, which surfaces as `configurationService.inspect('chat.tools.global.autoApprove').policyValue === false`. This is the **policy value**, not the setting value—the setting's own default is already `false` and carries no restriction.

Invariant: that policy restricts only elevated **approval** values. Agent Host `mode='autopilot'` must remain selectable and seedable; it runs within the permitted approval level, so tool calls still route through the session's approval level. Auto-approving in Autopilot to make it work would defeat the policy and is not an acceptable fix.

### Problem

The invariant holds in the current source, but is unpinned in the two paths most likely to regress—the new-session config seeds, where the approvals clamp and mode resolution sit side by side:

- `baseAgentHostSessionsProvider._initialNewSessionConfig` (Agents window): approvals are clamped while mode is resolved independently.
- `AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService._getInitialConfig` (editor window): no direct coverage today.

Already covered elsewhere and out of scope: `copilotAgent.getAutonomousSessionConfig` and `isPolicyBlockedCompletionAction`.

### Acceptance criteria

1. In `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`, with an auto-approve policy value of `false` and `chat.defaultConfiguration = { mode: 'autopilot', approvals: 'allowAll' }`, creating a session forwards `mode: 'autopilot'` and `autoApprove: 'default'`.
2. Extend the remembered Agent Host config migration coverage with a policy-restricted variant: remembered `autoApprove: 'autopilot'` still forwards `mode: 'autopilot'` and `autoApprove: 'default'`. This pins migration-before-clamp ordering.
3. Add coverage for `AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService._getInitialConfig`: mode passes through and approvals clamp under policy. Its seeded object also contains `isolation: 'folder'`.

### Non-goals

- No production behavior change unless a test reveals a violation; any fix must keep the clamp scoped to `SessionConfigKey.AutoApprove`, never the mode axis.
- The local/legacy chat Autopilot **permission level** remains bundled with auto-approval and intentionally policy-disabled. Do not change `permissionPickerActionItem`, `permissionPicker`, or `copilotChatSessionsProvider._defaultPermissionLevel`.

title: sessions: govern single-pane bottom panel at workbench level, remember its view per session
body:
## What

In the **single-pane** layout, the bottom panel is now handled like the side pane:

- **Visibility** is governed at the **workbench level** (not per session) and persisted across reloads.
- **Which view** the panel shows is remembered **per session** and restored on session switch or when the panel is revealed — never forcing the panel open (restoring a view while the panel is hidden would reveal it).
- A session with **no remembered view defaults to the Terminal**.

The **classic** layout is unchanged: it still remembers panel *visibility* per session and lets the view follow the global last-active.

## How

A single `_isPanelVisibilityPerSession` gate on `BaseLayoutController` drives both scopes — they are inverse, never both:

- `true` (classic): panel **visibility** is per session (`[B1]`).
- `false` (single-pane): panel **view** is per session instead (`[B6]`), persisted as `panelViewContainerId`.

`_syncPanelView` restores the remembered view (falling back to `TERMINAL_VIEW_ID`) only while the panel is already visible, via the session-switch autorun and a `PANEL_PART` visibility listener. Workbench-level panel visibility is saved/restored in `workbench.ts` alongside the other parts, gated on the single-pane layout.

## Notes for reviewers

- The single-pane controller overrides just the one `_isPanelVisibilityPerSession` flag; everything else derives from it.
- Spec updated in `baseSessionLayoutController.md` (`[B1]`, `[B6]`).
- Tests: added `[B6]` coverage (restore on switch/reveal, does not force the panel open while hidden, persistence + reload, Terminal default) and `[B1]` coverage for the workbench-level single-pane behavior. Full `BaseLayoutController` suite passes; typecheck and hygiene clean.

title: agent host: expose MCP support assessment
body:
## Summary

- Adds an internal, refcounted support scope that VS Code consumers can query before or during a Copilot CLI Agent Host session.
- Makes every known MCP server's source, client enablement, workspace applicability, delivery owner, compatibility, and reason codes available in one reactive snapshot.
- Includes installed servers disabled before runtime registration and waits for the initial installed-server inventory before resolving the first snapshot.
- Reports when discovery, MCP access, or customization policy limits coverage.
- Integrates the support assessment with customization migration as a binary supported/not-supported result, including discovery and coverage metadata.
- Reuses the same delivery resolver as the real forwarding path so reported support stays aligned with Agent Host behavior.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Consumer[VS Code consumer] --> Scope[MCP support scope]
    Inventory[MCP runtime and installed inventory] --> Scope
    Scope --> Snapshot[Reactive support snapshot]
    Snapshot --> Migration[Customization migration]
    Snapshot --> Decision[Other presentation or routing decisions]
```

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Workbench consumers could inspect servers already published by an active Agent Host session, but they had no client-side query that answered which configured servers were known before session creation, how each server would reach the host, or why a configuration could not be represented. Servers disabled by MCP access could also be absent from the runtime registry entirely.

The customization migration service also had no way to report whether discovered MCP servers were compatible with an Agent Host harness.

### Support assessment

`IAgentHostActiveClientService.acquireMcpServerSupportScope(sessionType, roots)` returns a shared scope for Copilot CLI harnesses. A one-shot consumer waits for `whenResolved()`, reads `scope.support.get()`, and disposes the scope; reactive consumers can observe `support` while retaining the same disposable reference.

The snapshot exposes per-server source metadata, enablement, applicability to the requested working directories, delivery path, compatibility, and structured incompatibility reasons. It also exposes lazy-discovery completeness and coverage flags for MCP access and strict customization policy.

The assessment merges the runtime MCP registry with the installed-server inventory so access-disabled configurations remain visible. `IMcpWorkbenchService.whenInitialLocalMcpServersLoaded` prevents the first support snapshot from treating the asynchronously populated installed inventory as empty. Initial query failures are logged and settle readiness so later refreshes do not repeatedly reject.

Collection provenance distinguishes VS Code user, remote, workspace, workspace-folder, root `.mcp.json`, extension, plugin, and externally discovered sources such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf.

### Customization migration integration

`CustomizationMigrationType.McpServers` adds a discriminated MCP migration result. The browser-layer implementation acquires the support scope, waits for resolution, filters servers outside the requested roots, maps exact `supported` compatibility to `supported: true`, and collapses partial, unsupported, and unknown compatibility to `false`.

The migration result also carries `discoveryComplete` and snapshot-wide MCP access/customization policy coverage flags. Enablement remains independent from compatibility.

The concrete migration service moved from `chat/common` to `chat/browser/aiCustomization` because it now injects the browser-layer `IAgentHostActiveClientService`. The shared service contract and DTOs remain in `chat/common`.

### Behavior and constraints

- The utility is an internal workbench API, not an extension API.
- `undefined` roots preserve unknown workspace applicability; an empty root array means there is no workspace.
- Enablement, applicability, delivery, and compatibility are independent. A disabled server can still have a supported configuration.
- Delivery distinguishes client-forwarded, runtime-discovered, plugin-provided, provider-built-in, not-delivered, and unknown cases.
- Partial and unsupported results explain ignored environment files, sandbox settings, development mode, OAuth client configuration, unresolved variables, interaction requirements, unsupported source locations, and unloaded definitions.
- Support scopes are created only when requested, shared by normalized session type and roots, refreshed when their inputs change, and disposed after their final consumer releases them.

### Review context

The main review boundary is consistency between support reporting and actual MCP forwarding. Both paths share delivery resolution, while enablement and disabled installed-server synthesis remain reporting-only so regular forwarding does not pay for diagnostic state.

The customization migration integration intentionally exposes only binary compatibility for now while preserving completeness and coverage metadata needed to interpret that result.

</details>

title: GitHub Copilot inline suggestions fail when parent directory name contains a space on Windows
body:
# GitHub Copilot inline suggestions fail when parent directory name contains a space on Windows

## Description

GitHub Copilot ghost-text/inline completions stop working when the active file is inside a directory whose name contains a space.

The issue is reproducible with a minimal Python file in a clean directory.

Removing the space from the directory name immediately restores inline suggestions.

## Steps to reproduce

Create these two directories:

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\
├── TEST\
│   └── test.py
│
└── TEST TEST\
    └── test.py
```

Both `test.py` files contain exactly:

```python
# calculate the factorial of a number
```

Open `D:\copilot-space-test` in VS Code.

### Test 1 — directory without a space

Open:

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py
```

Press Enter after the comment and start typing:

```python
def 
```

Copilot provides an inline/ghost-text completion as expected.

### Test 2 — directory containing a space

Open the identical file:

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST\test.py
```

Press Enter after the comment and type:

```python
def 
```

No inline suggestion is provided.

The Copilot status menu reports:

```text
No inline suggestion available
```

### Test 3 — rename the directory

Rename:

```text
TEST TEST
```

to something without a space, for example:

```text
TEST-TEST
```

Open the same `test.py` again.

Inline suggestions immediately start working.

## Reproduction commands

The test environment can be created in PowerShell with:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST" | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST" | Out-Null

'# calculate the factorial of a number' | Set-Content "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py"
Copy-Item "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py" "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST\test.py"

code "D:\copilot-space-test"
```

## Expected behavior

Copilot inline suggestions should work in both directories.

## Actual behavior

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py
→ inline suggestions work

D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST\test.py
→ no inline suggestions
```

The only relevant difference is the space in the parent directory name.

## Additional information

- The issue is not specific to Python. I originally encountered it with `.tex` files as well.
- It occurs in a clean test directory outside OneDrive.
- I have reproduced it with multiple directory names containing spaces.
- Copilot Chat and Next Edit Suggestions continue to work.
- This appears to be a regression: inline suggestions previously worked in my existing directories containing spaces.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.135.0
- OS: Windows 11 x64 (`Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200`)
- GitHub Copilot: Pro

title: Drive chat input notifications from an experiment
body:
Adds a `chatNotifications` treatment carrying a JSON payload, so a chat input notification can be authored or retired without shipping code.

The payload describes the title, description, action buttons and who sees it. A switch-to-model action can also carry model configuration, such as a thinking level or the Auto routing tier.

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "notifications": [{
    "id": "auto-tier-nudge",
    "severity": "info",
    "title": "Auto now picks stronger models",
    "description": "Auto routes each request to the best available model.",
    "match": { "sessionTypes": ["copilotcli"], "excludeSelectedModels": ["auto"] },
    "actions": [
      { "id": "learn", "kind": "command", "label": "Learn More",
        "commandId": "vscode.open", "args": ["https://aka.ms/x"] },
      { "id": "switch", "kind": "switchToModel", "label": "Switch to Auto",
        "model": "auto", "config": { "tier": "max" } }
    ],
    "dismissible": true,
    "autoDismissOnMessage": false
  }]
}
```

**Authoring.** `id` is a stable lowercase id used for telemetry and to remember dismissal, so changing it re-shows reworded copy. `title` and `description` carry the text, in English, since ExP serves locale-specific payloads through its own audience filters. `severity` is `info`, `warning` or `error` and defaults to info. `match` decides who sees it and must narrow at least one dimension; all three lists are fuzzy, so `sessionTypes` takes either a session type such as `agent-host-claude` or the harness behind it such as `copilotcli`, while `selectedModels` and `excludeSelectedModels` take a model's id, family, display name or vendor and respectively require or suppress the current selection. `actions` holds up to three buttons of kind `command` (any command id plus args), `openModelPicker`, or `switchToModel`, whose `model` selector must resolve to exactly one available model and whose optional `config` sets keys from that model's own schema. `dismissible` and `autoDismissOnMessage` are booleans; the second hides the notification once the user sends a message and lets it return next window, so it is the gentler setting rather than a permanent dismissal.

Notes for reviewers:

- A switch-to-model nudge should skip users already on its target, which a positive allow-list cannot express. That is what `excludeSelectedModels` is for, and the example above reads as "Copilot CLI users not already on Auto".
- `config` key names come from the model's publisher and differ between them (`thinkingLevel`, `reasoningEffort`, `tier`). Keys a model does not declare are dropped and logged, so an author sees why a button half-worked. Auto's `tier` also needs `chat.autoMode.tiers.enabled`, which is itself experiment-gated.
- The parser never throws and rejects a bad payload whole. Removing the assignment is the kill switch; an empty `notifications` list retires a notification immediately.
- Envelope parsing, selector matching and dismissal storage are now shared with the feedback survey and the promo notification, which is most of the churn in existing files.

Part of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8949

title: Restore the expandable changed-files list in the chat turn changes summary
body:
Clicking `N files changed` (or the chevron after the diff stats) on a completed agent turn no longer expanded the list of individual changed files. #332759 set out to remove the inline preview pill (`N files changed +A -B | SomeFileToPreview`) but also replaced the disclosure in `ChatTurnPillsContentPart` with a plain `<div>` header, so `N files changed` became an inert `<span>` and only the `+X -Y` counts button stayed interactive. Tests and fixtures were updated in the same commit, so nothing flagged the loss.

This restores the disclosure while keeping the preview removal.

### `chatTurnPillsPart.ts`
- Header is a `<summary>` inside `<details class="checkpoint-file-changes-disclosure">` again.
- Re-added the chevron, with the `expanded` class and `aria-expanded` synced on `toggle`, and the header `aria-label` summary.
- Re-added the file list via the shared `renderChangesSummaryFileList` — the same list the checkpoint summary uses.
- Re-added the `ChatCollapsibleContentPart.userToggleEvent` dispatch on header click, so `ChatListWidget` re-measures and anchors the row instead of auto-scrolling on expand.
- The counts button keeps `dom.EventHelper.stop(e, true)`, so it opens the Changes view without toggling the disclosure.

### `chat.css`
- Dropped the `.chat-turn-pills-part` `cursor: default` and hover-colour-reset overrides that made the header non-interactive; pointer cursor, hover foreground and chevron reveal come back.

### Tests and fixtures
- `hasDisclosure` is true again, plus a test covering expand-from-header (open state, chevron/aria state, rendered rows, exactly one `userToggleEvent`) and the counts button opening changes without toggling.
- Restored the `ChangesOnly_Expanded` component fixture.

### Deliberately unchanged
- The inline preview pill, its `getFileEditsForRequest` usage and the per-row "Preview" actions stay removed. `IChangesSummaryFileListOptions.getRowActions` remains unused in production — straightforward to wire back if wanted.
- The authoritative `getChangeStatsForRequest` counts from #332759 still drive the header.

### Known divergence, worth a follow-up
Header counts read `getChangeStatsForRequest` (Changes-view turn changeset, last turn only, workspace-filtered) while the list reads `getChangesForRequest` (unfiltered). For the last turn these can disagree, so the row count may not match the `N files changed` label when a turn touches files outside the workspace. Aligning them needs the stats API to expose the authoritative file list, which is beyond a restore.

3. Right-click the word.
4. Confirm suggestions appear above the edit items, clicking one replaces the word, and **Add to Dictionary** clears the underline.
5. Right-click a correctly spelled word and confirm the extra items are absent.
6. Repeat in an untrusted workspace or with `workbench.browser.dataStorage: ephemeral`. Confirm suggestions still work and **Add to Dictionary** is not shown.

title: chat: show one OS notification when a session has no more work
body:
chat: show one OS notification when a session has no more work

Agent host sessions can be open in the editor window and the agents window at the
same time. This caused two problems with the OS notifications. A "finished" toast
came when a response ended, even if more requests were in the queue. A session that
was open in two windows made one toast from each window.

- Adds an idle observable in the chat window notifier. It combines the request
  state, the input state, and the count of queued requests. The notifier shows the
  toast only when the session has no more work. A 500ms delay prevents a toast in
  the short gap between two queued turns.
- Makes the chat window notifier the only source of toasts in a window. It now
  shows the toast for needed input and for the idle state. The toast in the chat
  accessibility service is removed. That service keeps the accessibility signal and
  the ARIA announcement.
- Limits the sessions window notifier to sessions that have no chat model in this
  window. Sessions with a model are the responsibility of the chat window notifier,
  which knows about the queue.
- Adds a dedupe key to the toast options. The main process does not show a second
  toast while a toast with the same key is on the screen. This prevents duplicate
  toasts from two windows for one session.
- Delays the toast 250ms in a window that does not show the session. The window
  that shows the session makes its toast first, so a click opens the window that
  the user worked in.
- Delays the completed toast 1500ms in the sessions window notifier. A session with
  no chat model here gives no queue information, so the delay prevents a toast in
  the gap between two queued turns. See
  https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/issues/426 for the permanent fix.

title: Fix stale Open Recent entries after failed open on macOS
body:
Fixes #332665

## Problem

On macOS, opening a deleted folder from **File > Open Recent** shows the "Path does not exist" dialog, but the entry stays in the menu when all editor windows are closed.

The MRU store is updated correctly (`removeRecentlyOpened` runs on failure), but the main-process `Menubar` keeps serving stale cached menu data because it never listens to `onDidChangeRecentlyOpened`. With zero windows open, no renderer is alive to push fresh menu data.

## Fix

- Add `pruneRecentMenuItems()` to walk cached menu trees and drop recent items no longer in the MRU list.
- In `Menubar`, listen to `workspacesHistoryMainService.onDidChangeRecentlyOpened`, prune stale entries from `menubarMenus`, persist the updated cache, and rebuild the native menu.

This is self-healing: even if the cached menu was stale at startup, clicking the dead entry removes it from history, triggers pruning, and rebuilds the menu.

## Tests

- `src/vs/platform/menubar/test/common/menubar.test.ts` — prunes absent folder/workspace/file items, recurses into submenus, leaves actions/separators untouched, returns `false` when nothing changed.

## Manual repro

1. Open a local folder so it appears under File > Open Recent.
2. Close the VS Code window, delete the folder in Finder.
3. From the macOS menu bar, File > Open Recent > choose the deleted folder.
4. Dismiss the "Path does not exist" dialog.
5. Open File > Open Recent again — entry should be gone.

## Description

At times where the streaming output is more condensed, there's no visible affordance to know whether the agent is still working. The only way to tell is by checking whether the stop button is showing.

The progress shimmer around the input area should still be running during these condensed streaming states, but it appears to not be showing up.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c516111c-15d5-4ad2-9ccf-302131cdcb2b)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start an agent session where the streaming output is condensed (few visible tokens/updates).
2. Observe that there is no loading indicator (e.g. shimmer around the input area) shown.
3. The only working-state indicator is the presence of the stop button.

## Expected behavior
The progress shimmer around the input area should continue to indicate that the agent is actively working, even when streaming output is condensed.

## Actual behavior
No loading indicator is shown in this state, making it unclear whether the agent is still working.

fix: make ahead-of-time terminal executable resolution best-effort (fixes #333012)
body:
### Summary On a remote (SSH) terminal, `TerminalInstance` eagerly resolves the shell executable ahead of process creation as an optimization. This path calls `TerminalProcessManager.getBackendOS()`, which throws `Failed to get remote environment for remote authority "..."` when the remote agent environment cannot be fetched yet (connection still establishing or dropped). Because the call runs inside the non-disposed `_xtermReadyPromise.then()` chain, the rejection escapes as unhandled-error telemetry even though the OS/executable is re-resolved later through the normal process-creation path. Affects ~117 users across two sibling buckets on Windows and Mac. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333012 Recommended reviewer: `@meganrogge` ### Culprit Commit No single culprit commit could be pinned. The throw at `terminalProcessManager.ts:594` and the eager-resolution consumer at `terminalInstance.ts` both predate the regression window: `git blame` attributes the `getBackendOS` throw to `f7b171120126` (Megan Rogge, 2022-01-25). The regression-scan comment notes the bucket ID drifts across insider builds throughout the 1.134→1.135 window with no clean first-bad commit, indicating a **pre-existing** latent bug surfacing more frequently (likely a re-bucketing / environmental shift in remote-connection timing) rather than a code regression. Per the pre-existing classification, no culprit is named. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Xterm as _xtermReadyPromise.then participant Instance as TerminalInstance participant PM as TerminalProcessManager participant Remote as RemoteAgentService Xterm->>Instance: eager executable resolution (optimization) Instance->>PM: getBackendOS() PM->>Remote: getEnvironment() Note over Remote: ⚠️ Root cause:
returns null when SSH
remote env unavailable Remote-->>PM: null Note over PM: 💥 throw Error:
Failed to get remote environment PM-->>Instance: rejected promise Note over Instance: instance not disposed →
escapes as unhandled telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts` | crash site | L594 (from stack): `throw new Error("Failed to get remote environment for remote authority ...")` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts` | root cause (consumer) | L557-L558: eager optimization awaits `getBackendOS()`, which throws when the remote env is not yet available, inside the non-disposed `.then()` chain | ### Repro Steps 1. Open a workspace connected to an SSH remote (`ssh-remote+`). 2. Enable terminal shell integration (default) and ensure the shell launch config has no explicit executable. 3. Create a terminal while the remote connection is unavailable or still being established (e.g. the SSH host is briefly unreachable). 4. `getBackendOS()` rejects because `getEnvironment()` returns null; the rejection escapes the eager-resolution path and is reported to error telemetry. Because it depends on remote-connection timing it is non-deterministic; interrupting/degrading the SSH connection during terminal creation increases the likelihood. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts`: the ahead-of-time executable resolution is purely an optimization; the same OS/executable resolution happens again through the normal path in `_createProcess()` → `createProcess()`. The eager block is now wrapped so that if `getBackendOS()` (or the profile resolution) rejects, `os` is reset to `undefined` and a `logService.trace` note is recorded, letting terminal creation continue normally instead of surfacing an unhandled error. This is a consumer-side fix at the optimization site — the producer's deliberate throw (which still feeds telemetry for genuinely required remote-env fetches) is left intact, and no `logService.error` call is removed. The fix targets the code that invokes a throwing call opportunistically, not the crash site itself. **Why this fix works**: after this change, the eager-resolution branch at `terminalInstance.ts:557` can no longer let a `getBackendOS()` rejection escape into the non-disposed `.then()` chain, because the awaited calls are contained and a failure downgrades the optimization to a no-op that the later `_createProcess()` path recovers from. **Alternatives considered**: adding a guard at `getBackendOS()` to return `OS` instead of throwing was rejected — it would silence a legitimate error for callers that genuinely require the remote OS and remove diagnostic signal from the telemetry pipeline. Removing the eager-resolution optimization entirely was rejected as a broader behavior change than the regression warrants. ### Recommended Owner `@meganrogge` — terminal-area team member with write access, highly active (commits landed the same day), and the original author of the `getBackendOS` crash-site code (`f7b171120126`). > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33105062922) · opus48 · 349.5 AIC · ⌖ 11.9 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: make ahead-of-time terminal executable resolution best-effort (fixes #333012)
body:
### Summary On a remote (SSH) terminal, `TerminalInstance` eagerly resolves the shell executable ahead of process creation as an optimization. This path calls `TerminalProcessManager.getBackendOS()`, which throws `Failed to get remote environment for remote authority "..."` when the remote agent environment cannot be fetched yet (connection still establishing or dropped). Because the call runs inside the non-disposed `_xtermReadyPromise.then()` chain, the rejection escapes as unhandled-error telemetry even though the OS/executable is re-resolved later through the normal process-creation path. Affects ~117 users across two sibling buckets on Windows and Mac. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#333012 Recommended reviewer: `@meganrogge` ### Culprit Commit No single culprit commit could be pinned. The throw at `terminalProcessManager.ts:594` and the eager-resolution consumer at `terminalInstance.ts` both predate the regression window: `git blame` attributes the `getBackendOS` throw to `f7b171120126` (Megan Rogge, 2022-01-25). The regression-scan comment notes the bucket ID drifts across insider builds throughout the 1.134→1.135 window with no clean first-bad commit, indicating a **pre-existing** latent bug surfacing more frequently (likely a re-bucketing / environmental shift in remote-connection timing) rather than a code regression. Per the pre-existing classification, no culprit is named. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Xterm as _xtermReadyPromise.then participant Instance as TerminalInstance participant PM as TerminalProcessManager participant Remote as RemoteAgentService Xterm->>Instance: eager executable resolution (optimization) Instance->>PM: getBackendOS() PM->>Remote: getEnvironment() Note over Remote: ⚠️ Root cause:
returns null when SSH
remote env unavailable Remote-->>PM: null Note over PM: 💥 throw Error:
Failed to get remote environment PM-->>Instance: rejected promise Note over Instance: instance not disposed →
escapes as unhandled telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts` | crash site | L594 (from stack): `throw new Error("Failed to get remote environment for remote authority ...")` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts` | root cause (consumer) | L557-L558: eager optimization awaits `getBackendOS()`, which throws when the remote env is not yet available, inside the non-disposed `.then()` chain | ### Repro Steps 1. Open a workspace connected to an SSH remote (`ssh-remote+`). 2. Enable terminal shell integration (default) and ensure the shell launch config has no explicit executable. 3. Create a terminal while the remote connection is unavailable or still being established (e.g. the SSH host is briefly unreachable). 4. `getBackendOS()` rejects because `getEnvironment()` returns null; the rejection escapes the eager-resolution path and is reported to error telemetry. Because it depends on remote-connection timing it is non-deterministic; interrupting/degrading the SSH connection during terminal creation increases the likelihood. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts`: the ahead-of-time executable resolution is purely an optimization; the same OS/executable resolution happens again through the normal path in `_createProcess()` → `createProcess()`. The eager block is now wrapped so that if `getBackendOS()` (or the profile resolution) rejects, `os` is reset to `undefined` and a `logService.trace` note is recorded, letting terminal creation continue normally instead of surfacing an unhandled error. This is a consumer-side fix at the optimization site — the producer's deliberate throw (which still feeds telemetry for genuinely required remote-env fetches) is left intact, and no `logService.error` call is removed. The fix targets the code that invokes a throwing call opportunistically, not the crash site itself. **Why this fix works**: after this change, the eager-resolution branch at `terminalInstance.ts:557` can no longer let a `getBackendOS()` rejection escape into the non-disposed `.then()` chain, because the awaited calls are contained and a failure downgrades the optimization to a no-op that the later `_createProcess()` path recovers from. **Alternatives considered**: adding a guard at `getBackendOS()` to return `OS` instead of throwing was rejected — it would silence a legitimate error for callers that genuinely require the remote OS and remove diagnostic signal from the telemetry pipeline. Removing the eager-resolution optimization entirely was rejected as a broader behavior change than the regression warrants. ### Recommended Owner `@meganrogge` — terminal-area team member with write access, highly active (commits landed the same day), and the original author of the `getBackendOS` crash-site code (`f7b171120126`). > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33105062922) · opus48 · 349.5 AIC · ⌖ 11.9 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. title: Context-size configuration is lost for extension-provided models in Agent Host
body:
Hi! I’m working on a `LanguageModelChatProvider` for Vercel AI Gateway, and I ran into what looks like an Agent Host projection gap.

I first noticed this through the product: the Vercel models work in both normal Chat and a Local Agent Host session, but the Context Size dropdown only appears in normal Chat.

The provider already includes `contextSize` choices in the model's `configurationSchema`. Normal Chat renders those choices and passes the selection back to the provider. When the same model is used through Agent Host, the model still appears and works, but that configuration is no longer available.

## Reproduction

1. Install an extension that contributes a language model with `configurationSchema.properties.contextSize`.
2. Select the model in normal Chat and confirm that Context Size is available.
3. Start a Local session from the Agents view.
4. Select the same model and open its configuration.

The Context Size control is missing in the Agent Host session.

I think this is adjacent to #328336 and #320824. #329892 is also close, although I’m not sure it’s exactly the same question: that issue is about declaring context-size choices in `chatLanguageModels.json`, while in this case the extension provider has already declared them and normal Chat can render them.

Looking through the current path, it seems like Agent Host reconstructs the reasoning-effort configuration explicitly, but doesn't carry the provider's context-size choices—or its configuration schema more generally. I may be missing a supported hook here.

What is the intended boundary? Should Agent Host preserve the model configuration supplied by an extension provider, or should context size become another explicit capability carried through the bridge?

If there’s already a supported way for a provider extension to make this configuration available in Agent Host, I’d be happy to use it.

# Suggestion: Test coverage for Copilot chat in floating (auxiliary) windows

- **Drafted:** 2026-08-27
- **Type:** Suggestion for `microsoft/vscode` (test coverage / regression prevention)
- **Affected area:** Auxiliary (floating) window rendering of Copilot chat and related editor widgets

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

First, thank you for VS Code — it is a pleasure to use, and floating windows plus Copilot chat are a great combination. This is offered gently as a small suggestion, not a complaint.

Why this matters to us: each of these incidents tends to cost roughly half a day of troubleshooting or hunting for a workaround. VS Code is such a powerful and useful IDE that we simply cannot afford not to use it. Our corporate IT team maintains a baseline version as a safe home to fall back to, but that build usually lags well behind and misses helpful features from the latest release — so staying current matters to us. That is why a little extra test coverage around this area would go a long way toward stability.

Over about two weeks we happened to run into two core issues, both while using Copilot chat in a floating/auxiliary window, and both seemingly from the same underlying cause: DOM nodes created against the **main** window's `document` while the component is rendered inside a **child/auxiliary** window (`auxiliaryWindowService.ts` guards `document.createElement` on aux-window documents, so such a call throws instead of rendering).

Because it surfaced at more than one call site, it might be worth a little more automated coverage for the auxiliary-window path. A few ideas:

- Chat session editor in an auxiliary window — moving a chat session editor into an auxiliary window and checking the pane renders without throwing (the `createDormantHost` / "Move to New Window" case).

Thank you to the Microsoft engineering team for their continued craftsmanship. The notes below are offered gently, only in the hope of being helpful.

---

The sections below are supporting detail for this repository's records.

## Summary

Over about two weeks we happened to run into two VS Code core issues, both while using Copilot chat in a floating/auxiliary window, and both seemingly from the same underlying cause: code that creates DOM nodes against the **main** window's `document` while the component is rendered inside a **child/auxiliary** window. `auxiliaryWindowService.ts` intentionally guards `document.createElement` on aux-window documents (so `x instanceof HTMLElement` keeps working), so such a call throws instead of rendering.

Because it surfaced at more than one call site, it may be that the auxiliary-window path could benefit from a little more automated coverage. This is just a suggestion, not a critique.


## A gentle suggestion

If it seems worthwhile, some automated coverage for Copilot chat rendered in an auxiliary (floating) window might help catch this pattern early. A few ideas:

title: Open Dev Container agent sessions in the editor
body:
## Summary

Fixes **Open in Editor** for Agent Host sessions running in a Dev Container. The action now translates the Agent Host workspace URI into the `vscode-remote://dev-container+...` URI expected by the Dev Containers extension.

Follow-up to #331934.

Tracking issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317380

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Use `dev-container+`, not `attached-container+`**: These sessions originate from a local source folder with a Dev Container configuration. Encoding that source folder lets the Dev Containers extension rediscover the configuration and reconnect using its normal resolver path.
- **Carry the source host folder explicitly**: The runtime Dev Container connection now retains `hostPath`; the container ID alone is not sufficient to construct a `dev-container+` authority.
- **Preserve the container workspace path**: Only the URI scheme and authority are translated. The Agent Host's remote path (for example `/workspaces/project`) remains the folder opened inside the container.
- **Match the extension's authority encoding**: The host path is UTF-8 hex encoded, matching `getDevContainerUri`. This safely preserves POSIX paths, Windows drive-letter paths, spaces, and explicitly supported WSL UNC paths.
- **Do not claim generic UNC-share support**: Dev Containers explicitly routes `\\wsl.localhost` / `\\wsl$` paths through WSL, while ordinary network-share UNC support is not reliable end to end.
- **Code OSS testing limitation**: The marketplace Dev Containers extension intentionally does not register its resolver without the Microsoft-only `vsda` dependency. The exact generated URI was therefore validated separately in official VS Code Insiders rather than bypassing that product check.

</details>

## Changes

- Retain the original local source folder on managed Dev Container Agent Host connections.
- Resolve Dev Container session workspaces to `vscode-remote://dev-container+<hex-host-path>/<container-path>`.
- Share Agent Host folder URI translation between remote provider types and the Open in Editor action.
- Add regression coverage for POSIX, Windows drive-letter, and WSL UNC source paths.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Focused `resolveRemoteAuthority` tests: 3 passing
- ESLint on all changed files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Live validation in VS Code Insiders 1.136.0 with Dev Containers 0.467.0: the resolver reused the running container and opened `/workspaces/test`

title: build: retry throttled Foundry downloads
body:
## Summary

- retry transient HTTP 408, 429, and 5xx responses from Foundry native dependency downloads
- honor `Retry-After` responses from Azure Artifacts
- bound retries to five attempts and cap delays at 30 seconds

## Why

The Foundry native dependency installer uses a single authenticated NuGet feed. A transient Azure Artifacts 429 therefore caused the ARMHF build to fail immediately with `Failed to download Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local.Core 1.2.3 from any feed`. The triggering merge appears unrelated; this makes the downloader resilient to the feed throttling exposed by that build.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- `node --experimental-strip-types --check build/dictation-runtime/nuget.ts`
- imported `build/dictation-runtime/nuget.ts` with Node type stripping

Full build type-check and ESLint could not run locally because this worktree does not have the existing TypeScript and ESLint dependencies installed.
